meaning:
μετα-σχηματίζω
[in LXX: 4Ma.9:22 * ;]
to change in fashion or appearance: with accusative of thing(s), τ. σῶμα, Php.3:21; mid., before εἰς, 2Co.11:13-14; before ὡς, 2Co.11:15; of a rhetorical device, to transfer by a fiction (Field, Notes, in l), before εἰς, 1Co.4:6.†
SYN.: μεταμορφόω, q.v (AS)

renderings.kjv: I have in a figure transferred

elsewhere.note: Now these things, brothers, I have in a figure transferred to myself and Apollos for your sakes, that in us you might learn not to think beyond the things…
For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as Christ’s apostles.
who will change the body of our humiliation to be conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working by which he is able even to subject all things…
